hook.line: Five things you need to learn SEO (on-screen title; the spoken track did not transcribe cleanly).
hook.visual: One-frame thumbnail: giant red '5' and 'THINGS YOU NEED TO LEARN SEO' beside him holding up an open hand; cut at 0.07 s to him at a desk raising five fingers.

beats.what: Thumbnail-style title card flashes, then he faces camera at a desk.
Red-and-white caption '5 THINGS YOU NEED TO LEARN SEO' appears as he raises five fingers.
Item 1 'Basic education' over b-roll of an open book and magnifying glass.
Rapid b-roll list: laptop, his own YouTube course channel, SEMrush/Ahrefs/WordPress logos, a clock for 'Time'.
Zoom punch on the clock graphic for item 5, time.
Back on camera counting on his fingers as he expands on the list.
Pink-washed b-roll of an office presenter beside a laptop chart.
Brief cutaway to a 'What is SEO?' definition screen.
On camera; a Black Friday 80% scholarship SEO course offer is pitched.
End card: profile photo, 'comment BLACK FRIDAY below and I'll send you the details', follow button.

why_it_works: A big red numeral and a raised open hand promise a short, countable list, so the viewer knows the cost of staying.
The whole list is shown in the first 15 s as quick labelled b-roll, then explained, so the payoff comes before the detail.
'Comment BLACK FRIDAY' turns the sale into comments (661), which the algorithm rewards and which give him a DM list.
weaknesses: After 16 s it settles into a long static desk shot (19.2 s longest shot) with almost no graphics.
There are no spoken-word captions (words on screen median 2), so sound-off viewers lose the explanation.
The second half is a course pitch, which the 0.44 loop score and the drop in visual change suggest loses viewers.
for_robert: Front-load the whole list as a 2-second-per-item montage with numbered labels, then explain each item; have Fred hold up the number for each item.
